question: A company started with 174 items. They multiplied by 7 times. They added 45 items. They doubled it, then doubled again. They multiplied by 5 times. Tom had fewer items. Sarah compared her inventory. They had extra stock beyond this. How many items?

A shop had 191 things. They removed 57 things. They removed 5 more. They multiplied by 6 times. They removed 96 things. The inventory at opening versus closing showed the change. They had 400 other items elsewhere. How many things remain?

A factory started with 61 units. They tripled production. They added 79 units. They multiplied by 9 times. They removed 2221 units for shipment. They removed 89 units for defects. They added 68 units from returns. The time tracking was in minutes converting to hours. How many units remain?

A gardener had 110 seeds. They added 20 seeds. They divided into 5 rows equally. They removed 15 seeds that didn't sprout. They multiplied the remaining by 7 for planning. Morning planting, afternoon watering, evening checking. Someone had a dozen seeds (word count). How many seeds for growth?
A warehouse had 71 items. They added 33 items. They added 40 items. They multiplied by 5 times. They multiplied by 7 times again. Someone ordered a dozen items separately. How many items?

A shop had 214 products. They removed 213 products. They multiplied by 5 times. They removed 4 products. They multiplied by 6 times. They multiplied by 8 times. Morning inventory, afternoon sales, evening recount with a dozen items mentioned. How many products?

A café had 50 drinks. They added 8 drinks. They multiplied by 5 times (five batches made). They added 63 drinks. They removed 252 drinks sold. They had a dozen cups available. The inventory at start versus end differed. How many drinks?

A school had 212 students. They added 24 students. They multiplied by 9 times for projections. They multiplied by 2 times (double-booked classes). They multiplied by 9 times again. David's class was smaller, Maria's was larger. How many students?

A baker had 81 loaves. They divided into 3 sections. They doubled the amount by baking more. They removed 44 loaves (sold). They removed 9 loaves (stale). They added 19 fresh loaves. Tom had fewer loaves. Maria had more. How many loaves?

A farmer had 55 crops. They added 7 crops. They added 28 crops. They added 37 crops. They removed 12 crops (harvested). They multiplied by 8 for next season planning. They removed 376 from projections. Morning weeding, afternoon planting, evening watering tracked separately. Tom's farm was smaller. Maria's was larger. Converting minutes to hours in time. How many crops?

A jeweler had 121 gems. They removed 1 gem. They divided by 4. They divided by 6. They added 45 gems. They added 33 gems. The pricing was in cents per gem converting to dollars. They had an extra dozen gems elsewhere. How many gems?

A student had 39 pens. They added 78 pens. They removed 48 pens (lost some). They divided by 3 for group distribution. They added 27 pens. Someone had a dozen pens. Morning inventory, afternoon purchase, evening counting. How many pens?

A collector had 27 items. They removed 13 items. They removed 9 items. They multiplied by 6 times. They multiplied by 6 times again. They added 67 items. Converting minutes to hours took time. The total progressed throughout the day. How many items?

A gardener had 56 seeds. They doubled the amount. They removed 7 seeds (defective). They added 25 seeds. They added 37 seeds. They added 6 seeds. Morning planting, afternoon watering, evening counting. How many seeds?

A store had 44 items. They added 71 items. They added 6 items. They multiplied by 5 times. They added 34 items. They added 50 items. They added 22 items. The accounting switched from minutes to hours format. How many items?

A farm had 46 animals. They removed 11 animals. They added 65 animals. They removed 41 animals. They removed 9 animals. They added 78 animals. They multiplied by 7 times. Morning count, afternoon additions, evening totals in time units. How many animals?

A baker had 35 loaves. They multiplied by 7 times. They multiplied by 7 again. They removed 1309 loaves (huge sale). They added 9 loaves (new batch). Someone had a dozen loaves elsewhere. The inventory at start and end showed progress. How many loaves?
A shop had 103 items. They removed 47 items. They removed 32 items. They multiplied by 8 times. They multiplied by 5 times. Someone had a dozen items. The other location had 50 items. How many items?

A farmer had 90 crops. They doubled them. They quadrupled by 4 times. They removed 633 crops (harvest). They added 56 crops (new planting). Morning tending, afternoon harvesting, evening replanting. 500 crops elsewhere didn't count. How many crops?

A baker had 223 loaves. They removed 194 loaves (sold). They added 28 loaves (baked). They added 69 loaves (fresh batch). They multiplied by 6 times for tomorrow's planning. They divided by 4 equal sections. The time tracking was in minutes converting to hours. Someone had a dozen loaves. The inventory progressed. How many loaves per section?

A factory had 67 items. They added 42 items. They multiplied by 4 times. They multiplied by 5 times. They divided by 5 (unsort). They multiplied by 8 times. They removed 2663 items. The time was in minutes converting to hours. How many items?

A student had 95 items. They added 37 items. They multiplied by 3 times. They added 35 items. They added 69 items. They removed 122 items. They added 4 items. Someone had a dozen items. There were 50 items elsewhere. How many items total?

A baker had 49 loaves. They doubled them. They added 24 loaves. They removed 19 loaves. They multiplied by 3 times. They multiplied by 5 times. They multiplied by 3 times again. Morning baking, afternoon sales, evening restocking. 15 loaves elsewhere. How many loaves?
A business had 236 dollars. They removed 203 dollars. They multiplied by 4 times. They removed 125 dollars. They removed 4 dollars. The account progressed from opening to closing. How much money?

A shop had 174 items. They multiplied by 4 times. They divided by 6 sections. They removed 62 items. They removed 23 items. They removed 5 items. They added 12 items. Morning inventory, afternoon sales, evening recount. 50 items elsewhere. How many items?
